implementation_notes: The Ruby AMQP client exposes the envelope as publish options plus a properties object on delivery: exchange.publish(payload, headers:, content_type:, correlation_id:, reply_to:, message_id:, type:) sets the AMQP properties, and the subscription block receives (delivery_info, properties, body) so the envelope never has to be parsed out of the payload. That replaces the classic wrapper class; a plain Hash envelope (or framework job arguments) is the fallback when no broker carries the metadata. Hand-roll serialization only for a fixed legacy wire format.
code_sketch:
exchange.publish(order.to_json,
                 headers: { "x-format" => "order/v2" },
                 content_type: "application/json",
                 correlation_id: cid,
                 reply_to: reply_queue.name)
# consumer: unwrap at the seam
queue.subscribe(block: true) do |_info, properties, body|
  handle(JSON.parse(body), properties.headers)
end
pitfalls: Header keys arrive as strings even when symbols were used at publish time; symbol lookups return nil without raising.
Bunny publishing is asynchronous unless publisher confirms are enabled: a broker rejection is silent unless you use a confirm-enabled channel.
Properties travel with the message and are redelivered verbatim on requeue, so a stale correlation id or reply_to can mislead the next hop.
